flashcard_questions.q: Which band recorded the song Africa?
On which album did the song Africa first appear?
In which year was Africa released as a single?
Who co-wrote Africa with Jeff Porcaro?
What is the time signature of Africa?
Which overall form does Africa use?
Which dynamic marking is used for the choruses of Africa?
Which key are the verses of Africa normally taken to be in?
Which key are the choruses of Africa clearly in?
How many bars of unpitched percussion open the recording before the scored introduction?
Which scale does the five-note ostinato of Riff b use?
Which is the only section of Africa where Riff a does not appear?
Why are the first three phrases of Verse 1 nine bars long?
flashcard_questions.a: Riff a enters as the vocal line ends in bar 8, adding an extra bar.

flashcard_questions.q: How are the African pitched percussion sounds in Africa actually produced?
flashcard_questions.a: On a synthesiser, not on real instruments.

flashcard_questions.q: In the slash chord B/F#, what does the letter after the slash show?

notes: 15 cards: 4 background fact cards (band, album, release year, co-writer), 5 element cards (time signature, form, dynamics, two keys), 4 structure/timing cards taken exactly as the content states them (8-bar percussion intro, 9-bar phrase reason, Riff a absence, Riff b scale), plus 2 misconception cards (synthesised African timbres, slash-chord notation). No lyrics quoted; sections named instead. Dropped flavour glossary terms (soft-rock, riff, ostinato, parallel motion) because they duplicate other decks in this unit or fail the exam-relevance test here.
